text:
maria: FYI incoming support ticket from AcmeCorp — they report APAC customers suddenly seeing ~700-900ms p99 and intermittent 401s. They pasted a few request-ids, blaming wrong-region routing. https://support.example/XYZ-123 :wave

alex: jumping in, can you drop one of their request-ids and a sample curl?

maria: request-id 01H7X2A9, sample header shows X-Region-Hint: apac-west. They say sometimes they get 200 from apac, sometimes 401 from eu. here's a raw log snippet we got from edge (redacted):
```
[2026-02-25T03:13:22Z] req=01H7X2A9 region=apac-west routed_to=eu-west-1 fallback_reason=affinity_ttl_expired auth_status=401 lat_ms=812
[2026-02-25T03:13:24Z] req=01H7X2A9 region=apac-west routed_to=apac-west auth_status=200 lat_ms=118
```

ben: opsbot shows routing_fallback_rate spike at 03:12 UTC across apac-west: https://grafana/alert/AB123 — looks correlated with a small routing policy change that went out in the 03:10 deploy window.

opsbot: alert: routing-service.fallback_rate > 5% (apac-west) — triggered at 2026-02-25T03:12:05Z

alex: can we rollback that routing policy change? who owns it?

sarah: I pushed a change to multi-fallback evaluation rules (PR #592) at 03:09 to tighten regional affinity. The intention was to prefer local model variants, but the matcher short-circuits when multiple fallbacks exist — skipped TTL check. Reverting now.

alex: rollback initiated at 03:32 UTC — rolling back to policy version v2026-02-25-0300.

maria: customer confirmed at 03:40: "latency back to normal, 200s stable". Our telemetry shows apac-west p99 dropped from ~820ms -> ~130ms. Support notified the customer and kept ticket open for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

ben: created incident doc /incidents/1987654321 (working draft) and pinned logs. setting severity to Sev2 while we root cause.

maria: repro steps for engineering (short):
1) curl -v -H "X-Region-Hint: apac-west" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
2) repeat ~20x with concurrent clients and check routed region header: X-Routed-Region
3) you'll see intermittent X-Routed-Region: eu-west-1 and corresponding 401s in ~5-8% of requests when affinity_ttl is hit

sarah: root cause summary: a logic bug in the fallback-evaluator (PR #592) caused the affinity TTL guard to be bypassed when a secondary fallback list was populated. result: some sticky sessions were evaluated as expired earlier than they should, causing cross-region fallbacks to take effect and hit EU auth cluster (401) or higher latency.

alex: mitigations done: 1) immediate rollback of PR #592 2) short-term increase of affinity TTL by +30s for apac-west via feature flag 3) pushed a hotfix unit test to cover multi-fallback TTL path.

maria: customer impact: AcmeCorp SaaS customers in APAC saw increased p99 and auth failures for ~20 minutes (03:12–03:32). No billing discrepancy reported but we saw a small spike in request retries.

ben: action items (owners):
- sarah: PR hotfix + add regression test (in progress) — due EOD 2026-02-25
- alex: add canary gate for routing-eval changes and update deploy checklist — due 2026-03-02
- infra: add metric alert for cross-region-auth-failures > 0.5% for 5 min — due 2026-02-26
- product/support: follow up with AcmeCorp with root cause and offer 1 mo credit (optional) — maria to own, due 2026-02-26

support-bot: incident severity changed to Sev2 by ben at 2026-02-25T04:00:00Z

maria: quick note for the postmortem: include exact deploy diff for PR #592, logs for the 03:12–03:32 window, and the canary plan for routing changes. I'll draft the postmortem and share the doc link here when ready.

alex: thanks team. tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-sre for visibility. Closing thread for now, will reopen if we see recurrence. :lock:
